fact: METHOD, and it is the volume-at-a-time grid sweep, not an index lookup name by name. Both digitised volumes were opened whole and every printed page read: 1993 Talisman (dlsc_ua_records/417, 144 leaves) and 1994 Talisman (dlsc_ua_records/418, 148 leaves). 84 portrait grid pages were identified from the page images and 1,982 name labels were parsed off them with their cell positions - 1,047 in the 1993 volume and 935 in the 1994. THE GRID PAGES ARE: 1993 pp. 20-21 graduates, 24-46 seniors, 48-54 juniors, 56-62 sophomores, 63-74 freshmen, 76-80 faculty and staff, with the TOP OF THE HILL feature pages interleaved at 25, 31, 35, 39, 47, 51, 55, 59, 67, 71 and 75 and carrying no portraits; 1994 pp. 22-47 by residence hall then Off-Campus, 57-70 by greek chapter, 79-80 faculty and staff. LAYOUT, verified against the page images rather than assumed. 1993: four portraits across, five rows deep, the twenty names set in ONE COLUMN down the LEFT margin in blocks of four against each grid row, alphabetical left to right - read off p. 78, whose second block is Anna Jo Johnson, Horace Johnson Jr., Cynthia Y. Jones, Kaveh Khatir against four faces F M F M. 1994: five across, six deep, the thirty names in ONE COLUMN down the RIGHT margin in blocks of five, alphabetical left to right - read off p. 59 and p. 63, where the alphabet runs unbroken down three blocks and then restarts at a fresh chapter heading. THE BACK INDEXES were then re-OCR'd column by column at 5x, because the pooled page OCR reads these four-column pages badly: the 1993 index had a hole running from Seebold straight to Templeton, losing the whole Sh-Sm-St-Ta run including every Smith. That gives 1,739 complete index entries for 1993 and 1,240 for 1994, with no gap anywhere in the alphabet. Every target was then matched in one pass against the grid labels, against the indexes, and against all 16,432 raw OCR items of both volumes, with one-edit tolerance on surnames and nickname expansion on first names. WHY THE ANSWER IS THIS THIN, and it is not a failure of the sweep. Two things. FIRST, neither book photographs the whole student body. The 1993 volume's People section is a paid-sitting selection - about 1,047 portraits including faculty - and the 1994 volume's is organised by residence hall and greek chapter and comes to about 935. Against a student body of some 15,000 that is roughly one student in fifteen, so the base rate of any given senator appearing is about 7 per cent whatever else is true. SECOND, and this is the bigger one: THE 1994 TALISMAN IS THE LAST BOOK WITH PORTRAIT GRIDS AND IT COVERS 1993-94. There is no 1995 volume - record 419 and its neighbours are the Xposure magazines, which carry no grids - and nothing after that until 2013. name: Evon A. Rajeivick Jr.
kind: not photographed, but the surname is corrected
fact: THE SPELLING IS WRONG IN THE ARCHIVE AND THE RIGHT ONE IS RAJEWICH. The sweep of the 1993 and 1994 Talismans put him at the alphabetical position Rains, Joe / Rajewich, Tammy / Ramon, San, and Rajewich is not a variant of anything - it is a real Western surname with a real bearer. The Herald then names the man himself twice, both times with the W spelling and both times with Junior as a forename rather than a suffix: on 4 November 1993, reporting the student protest against the tuition increase, it quotes "Junior Rajewich, a Brownsville junior" in the same paragraph as Scott Sivley, who is in the 1993 ASG group photograph; and the dean's list of 27 January 1994 prints "Jr. Rajewich". So the archive's Evon A. Rajeivick Jr. is Evon A. Rajewich Jr. of Brownsville, known as Junior, a junior in autumn 1993 and therefore a senior in the year the archive seats him as Jr. Off Campus Rep. FLAGGED, NOT FIXED, per this archive's rule. HE IS STILL NOT PHOTOGRAPHED. Neither volume indexes him under either spelling. The only Rajewich in either book is "Rajewich, Tammy 42", a woman on the 1993 senior portrait grid at printed p. 42, quite possibly a relation and certainly not him; the 1994 index runs Rahim, Mubina / Ramon, San with nothing between. Do not let Tammy's cell drift onto his name.
